pageCache.pageTitle: PSHE and RSHE - Subjects - Windrush C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
PSHE and RSHE
Our aim is for all children to gain the knowledge and skills required to make informed decisions within, and react appropriately and with confidence to situations or problems they will face throughout their lives. To this end we undertake to:-
Develop children’s skills and knowledge and encourage and enable them to apply these to their own lives.
Encourage children to consider the viewpoints of others and develop empathy for the feelings of others within a wide range of different situations.
Enable and encourage children to make informed choices by providing them with knowledge and skills to do so.
Build on and develop existing knowledge as children progress through the school.
Develop children's emotional literacy and provide them with a range of strategies to help them deal with challenging situations and feelings.
Teachers will use the both PSHE association and Family Links to support planning. They will also use Zones of Regulation to help the children improve their emotional literacy. This will provide them with daily opportunities to reflect on how they feel and equip them with toolkits that contain a range of strategies to deal with difficult emotions.
The Family Links programme provides the school with a framework to support families at home. Two members of staff have been trained to provide praenting courses using this framework. The link to the PSHE curriculum in school means children are recieving a consistent message at home and in school.
In addition to this, two members of staff are trained ELSAs (Emotional Literacy Support Assistants). They work with small groups of children or individuals to help them navigate and understand their emotions and the impact their actions can have on the emotions of others around them.

pageCache.pageTitle: Religious Education - Subjects - Windrush C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Religious Education
At Windrush CofE Primary School, RE has a significant role for the development of pupils’ spiritual, moral, social and cultural development. It promotes respect and open-mindedness towards others with different faiths and beliefs and encourages pupils to develop their sense of identity and belonging through self-awareness and reflection.
The principle aim of RE is to engage pupils in an inquiry approach where they can develop an understanding and appreciation for the expression of beliefs, cultural practices and influence of principal religions and worldviews in the local, national and wider global community.
We use the Oxfordshire Agreed Syllabus in collaboration with Discovery RE to ensure children are experiencing a rich curriculum. We study the six main religions across the school and encourage the children to understand their own opinions and those of others, and that these can be different.
We use artefacts, visits, videos and visitors to bring context to the curriculum. Our parents are heavily involved and are excited to share the religious and cultural experiences bringing rich diversity to our curriculum. This allows us to celebrate the community around us and everything they believe in.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music - Subjects - Windrush C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Music
At Windrush Primary School we encourage pupils to participate in a variety of musical experiences through which we aim to build up the confidence of all pupils.
Our teaching focuses on:
● Developing musical skills and concepts through listening, appraising, performing and composing.
● Developing social skills through cooperation with others in the shared experience of music making.
● Developing an understanding of musical traditions and developments in a variety of cultures
● Enabling children to understand how sounds are made and how music is made through a variety of instruments.
● Contributing to the promotion of pupils’ spiritual, moral, social and cultural development.
● Inspiring Christian values through the singing of hymns and spiritual songs.
Besides being a creative and enjoyable activity, music can be a highly academic and demanding subject. It is also important in helping children feel part of a community. Music can be a lifelong source of pleasure for many people; it is education for life.
We use the Charanga Music scheme, which is promoted by the Oxfordshire Music Service. This ensures progression and coverage of knowledge and skills across the school while giving children a rich diet of musical experiences.

pageCache.pageTitle: Art & Design - Subjects - Windrush C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Art & Design
At Windrush CE Primary School we believe that teaching and learning in Art is important because it stimulates creativity, imagination and inventiveness. The purpose of art education is to give pupils the skills, concepts and knowledge necessary for them to express responses to ideas and experiences in a visual or tactile form. It fires their imagination and is a fundamental means of personal expression.
Art enables children to communicate what they see, feel and think through the use of colour, texture, form, pattern and different materials and processes. It also enables them to explore ideas and meanings through the work of artists and designers. Windrush School places an important emphasis upon creative and emotional development. Art at Windrush makes a major contribution to these aspects of education as well as to the spiritual and cultural development of pupils.
Each child will be given a sketch book at the start of Year 1. They will use this to develop their artistic skills and show the progression of learning througout each project. This sketch book will go up through the school with the children so they can look back at the progress they have made.

pageCache.pageTitle: Physical Education - Subjects - Windrush C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Physical Education
At Windrush School, Physical Education is an integral part of our curriculum. We aim to inspire a generation of children that understand how to live helathily, are active and enjoy physical activites and sports.
We recognise the importance physical wellbeing plays in ensuring good overall wellbeing. This is discussed when looking at the zones of regulation and physical exercise is discussed as a strategy to help manage difficult emotions.
We offer a range of sports and activities to allow pupils to develop and flourish. Sport is for all, and everyone can enjoy and participate in sport.
We aim to deliver high quality teaching and learning opportunities that enable all pupils to achieve their best. This is delivered by a high quality and experienced sports coach alongside highly trained teachers.
We encourage pupils to display the school values of perserverance, respect and responsibility in all of their sporting endeavours. This is important as the school increasingly participates in inter-school competitions and sports festivals.
Extra curricular clubs are offered through the school and children are encouraged to take part in both these and sports clubs offered elsewhere.

pageCache.pageTitle: Nature and the Environment - Subjects - Windrush C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Nature and the Environment
At Windrush school we are passionate about learning outside. We feel it is crucial that the children in our care have access to a high quality nature education so that they understand the natural world we live in.
Due to the nature of the estate the school is in, a nature curriculum ensures teachers are actively planning opportunities for the children to experience close encounters with nature.
As the school grows, the children will be involved in the planning and development of the site, especially our nature area. They will be taught about plants which enourage pollinators and make links with their other learning such as sensory experiences involving living things (e.g. smelling lavendar, stroking lambs ears...).

pageCache.pageTitle: Computing - Subjects - Windrush C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Computing
Technology plays an increasingly important role in our lives. At Windrush, we want pupils to become masters of technology. We want to model and educate our pupils on how to use technology positively, responsibly and safely. We want our pupils to be able to be able to critically evaluate content, as well as create their own content. We want our pupils to become effective coders. We foster logical thinking and develop this into coding skills. Our pupils will become skilful computer scientists, able to transfer the skills they have learnt in computing across the curriculum.
We use the curriculum that has been written by TeachComputing to support the planning and teaching of computing. This ensures progression across the school of knowledge and skills.

pageCache.pageTitle: Design Technology - Subjects - Windrush C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Design Technology
At Windrush School, we ensure that DT lessons allow children to use their creativity and imaginations to design, make and assess real life products, considering the needs and wants of either themselves or the audience of their product.
DT lessons also bring in skills from Maths, Science, Computing, Engineering and Art. The cross curricular nature of our curriculum means that all students have the opportunitiy to engage in different areas of the design curriculum and have a good understanding of how these skills can help them later in life. We feel it is important that the children understand why they learn when they are at school and so the impact on life around them.
From the very first day children start in Nursery they are encouraged to tinker, explore and investigate materials, processes and the way things are made. This sparks their curiosity which feeds into their design, make and evaluate processes further up the school. We celebrate creativity by showcasing their modelling and designs across the school in class, collective worship and around the school building.

pageCache.pageTitle: English - Subjects - Windrush C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
English
English and the teaching of English is the foundation of our curriculum. Our main aim is to ensure that every single child becomes primary literate and progresses in the areas of reading, writing, speaking and listening. We ensure that English is not only taught as a discrete subject but that it is embedded throughout the curriculum. Through using high-quality texts, immersing children in vocabulary rich learning environments and ensuring curriculum expectations and the progression of skills are met, the children at Windrush will be exposed to a language rich, creative and a continuous English curriculum. This will not only enable them to become primary literate but will also develop a love of reading, creative writing and purposeful speaking and listening.
We want our children to write clearly, accurately and coherently, adapting their language and style in and for a range of contexts, purposes and audiences. We provide opportunities for children to communicate independent views and opinions, respond imaginatively and express feelings through spoken and written language.
We believe that all pupils should be encouraged to take pride in the presentation of their writing, in part by developing a neat, joined, handwriting style by the time they move to secondary school. We believe that all good writers refine and edit their writing over time, so we want children to develop independence in being able to identify their own areas for improvement in all pieces of writing, editing their work effectively during and after the writing process.
Our aim is to develop children’s love of reading for pleasure and for our children to read a wide range of books by different authors and challenge themselves within their choices. At Windrush we believe that all pupils should have the opportunity to be fluent, confident readers who are able to successfully comprehend and understand a wide range of texts. We want pupils to develop a love of reading, a good knowledge of a range of authors, and be able to understand more about the world in which they live through the knowledge they gain from texts. By the end of their time at primary school, all children should be able to read fluently, and with confidence, in any subject in their forthcoming secondary education. We do not put ceilings on what pupils can achieve in reading and we do not hold pre-conceptions about any pupils’ ability to make progress. We understand the importance of parents and carers in supporting their children to develop both word reading and comprehension skills, and so we want to encourage a home-school partnership which enables parents and carers to understand how to enhance the skills being taught in school through good quality texts.
We aim to recognise the language experiences of children at home and in the wider community and to increase children’s understanding of how language is used in the world beyond school.
The Opening Doors Approach
The school has taken part in the Opening Doors KS1 training with Julie Sargent. This approach uses high quality texts with ambitious vocabulary that enables children to experience the literary world in a way they may not be able to independently. Through access strategies, vocabulary lessons and purposeful writing, children learn to love to write and understand how they can make their own and others work even better. The school is now part of the Opening Doors Network with Bob Cox.
Read Write Inc. Phonics
Read Write Inc. phonics is the systematic synthetic phonics scheme that the school and RLT follow to ensure high quality teaching of phonics and early reading. The scheme provides excellent resources which cover all of the sounds needed to access the Year 1 phonics screening check. It also focuses on speeding up reading, fluency and comprehension so children are prepared for more challenging reads in year 2 and above. The children are regularly assessed and grouped according to their needs and level of challenge or support. These groups then enable adults to provide books for reading at home which closely match the children's phonological awareness. Staff have been trained in the application of this scheme and any new members of the school are provided with the same level of training or refresher training. The Read Write Inc. Spelling Zone will then be used to support the teaching of spelling in year 2 and above. This ensures continuity and means that children are able to attend to the learning rather than spending time learning new routines, gestures and expectations.

pageCache.pageTitle: Geography - Subjects - Windrush C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Geography
At Windrush Primary School, we want to instil in all pupils a sense of awe, wonder and excitement at the world around them through our teaching of Geography. Geography helps promote a sense of global citizenship in our pupils, because they learn not only where places are and what they are like, but about the people who live there and what life is like for them. Pupils learn how the world around them has been formed and build on their own experiences to take their knowledge from the very personal to the global.
This links closely with our Personal Development Curriculum to encourage children to become well rounded human beings who understand their role, not only in their community, but in the wider world around them.
Geographical enquiry and teaching of Geography at Windrush helps pupils understand the complicated, changing world around them and how natural and human elements have contributed to it, and how they will continue to do so in the future. Teachers are enthusiastic about learning outdoors and using the school grounds and local area to practice their fieldwork skills.

pageCache.pageTitle: History - Subjects - Windrush C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
History
At Windrush, we teach a broad and culturally rich History curriculum to all pupils, so that they can understand past events and how they shaped the world we live in today and the people who live around us. Our History curriculum is planned ambitiously for all key stage phases, with topics chosen that represent every aspect of life. These include local historical studies where pupils will understand more about the history of their personal surroundings, to global historical events which pupils can begin to understand and make comparisons with their own lives.
We intend for pupils to learn from a range of races, religions, genders and cultures in History, so that their cultural capital is broadened significantly beyond their own experiences. We offer pupils plentiful opportunities to discuss, debate, question and enquire about their History learning so as to shape them into thoughtful Historians.
Teaching aims to bring the past to life, even for the youngest children, through drama, visitors, educational visits, artefacts and exciting experiences. For example, children in year 1 visit Oxford Castle and Prison, learn about the history behind the Battle of Hastings and reenact this through drama. Pupils in year 2 learn about the Great Fire of London and recreate a histroically accurate street (in collaboration with their DT learning) which they then burn to create an accurate depiction of this event.

pageCache.pageTitle: Maths - Subjects - Windrush C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Maths
It is our intent to instil a love of mathematics within our pupils so that they are excited and engaged with their learning. We aim to provide meaning and purpose for the mathematical skills they are learning so that they understand the importance of the subject in their wider life, both now and in their adult lives.
Children should leave Windrush school with a comprehensive understanding of the maths stipulated within the national curriculum and have a fluent knowledge of number bonds, multiplication tables and number facts appropriate to their age. They will be able to tackle complex problems using strategies they have been taught to break the problem down and use a range of representations to help them understand what is being asked of them. Children should be able to reason about mathematical statements using a wide range of vocabulary which is tailored to the area of mathematics they are discussing.
They will feel confident in their knowledge to make links between their learning and to use manipulatives, diagrams and calculations as evidence to support their arguments. Pupils should have a strong understanding of how to use manipulatives to support their learning when they are attempting a new skill, feel less confident or are trying to prove or disprove a theory.
The school will be using the mastery approach and all new teachers will be trained so that they understand the 5 main principles of mastery.
Through this approach, all children will have access to the same learning opportunities and teachers will carefully support and scaffold learning so that it is tailored to children’s specific needs - e.g. using manipulatives when completing calculations rather than drawing representations. Support and scaffolding will be planned thoroughly to develop independent strategies and to ensure that there is no reliance on manipulatives. Children with exceptional SEN needs may be accessing specific additional provision, however this will only be the case for children who are significantly behind their year group expectations. Planning will ensure that children are stretched and challenged through questioning, problem solving, reasoning and investigation of maths. Mathematical talk and language development will give children the tools to discuss their learning, explain their answers and confidently ask and answer questions.
Teachers are now using Mastering Early Number form NCETM in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2 to ensure children have a rapid recall of the number facts that are appropriate for their age and stage of development. This will enable children to access more difficult tasks and to become confident mathematicians as they move up through the school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Personal Development and Extra Curricular Activities - Windrush C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Personal Development and Extra Curricular Activities
Windrush School promotes the exstensive personal development of it's pupils. We provide opportunities for pupils to develop their talents and interests and they have access to a wide and rich set of experiences.
Our personal development curriculum is carefully planned for each year group and helps to strengthen children's character and develops their understanding of how to be responsible for their school community and the wider world. It celebrates achievements both in and outside of school and ensures opportunities are provided for those who may not have access to such rich experiences at home.
Children's emotional literacy is supported through our PSHE and RSHE curriculum with individual and group interventions offered for those who may find managing their emotions more difficult. This is carefully planned alongside the Family Links parenting course to ensure children recieve a consistent message at home and school.
We ensure every child's personal development is a priority with well trained staff who come equipped with a range of skill sets to support children of all abilities and backgrounds.
Our partnership with parents and members of the local community broadens children's opportunities and helps them understand where their learning can take them.
We use our Christian and British values to help demonstrate how children can become kind, responsible and respectful citizens.
We have carefully selected resources and books to ensure children are able to see themselves and a wide range of cultures within the books they are reading.
Windrush Personal Development Plan

Breakfast/after-school clubs
We recognise the importance to parents of providing first-rate childcare before and after school. The school day runs from 8.45am until 3.15pm.
Vicky's After School Clubs provides wraparound care for Windrush children in Reception and upwards.
Breakfast club is available from 7.45am
After School Club is available until 5.15pm
For more information, see www.vickysafterschoolclub.co.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher's Welcome - Windrush C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
Windrush Church of England Primary School is a new school which opened in September 2021. Our beautiful building and fantastic facilities make us a special place for children to learn and flourish. We are committed to providing a broad, balanced, and rich curriculum that not only enables children to be successful academically, but also to enrich themselves personally, allowing them to make valuable and meaningful contributions to society.
Our school has a strong culture of aspiration for all where children are inspired and challenged to be the best that they can be. We aim to create an educational environment that allows children to develop the ability to question, reason and gain independence in their learning, nurturing their skills and talents and providing a wealth of experiences and opportunities beyond the classroom.
Our Christian ethos supports children’s moral, social and spiritual development and challenges and inspires our children to develop their potential and a strong moral character through our Christian values so they will be respectful, courageous and compassionate and learn to look beyond themselves for the good of their community and the world beyond.
Windrush runs extra-curricular activities after school which include sports clubs, music, dance and martial arts clubs, plus a wide variety of events throughout the year within the school and in partnership with other local schools. We also have wraparound care - a breakfast club and after school club for working parents.
We hope you will find much to inspire you in the following pages and encourage you to come and visit us to see our wonderful school for yourself.
Claire Doland

pageCache.pageTitle: School tours for Reception 2027 admissions - Announcements - Windrush C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Announcements
School tours for Reception 2027 admissions
Are you interested in sending your child to our Reception class in September 2027?
Admission to our school is through Oxfordshire County Council - more information on how to apply and key dates for the application process can be found on their web page www.oxfordshire.gov.uk/schools
We will hold 45 minute school tours for families on the following dates - to express an interest in attending please complete the form found here: School tour sign up
Thursday 1st October at 10am
Wednesday 14th October at 2pm
Thursday 5th November at 2pm
Monday 16th November at 10am
Tuesday 24th November at 10am
For any further information, please email the school office - office@windrushschool.org
